passages.scripture: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.

lines.text: God is merciful.
Paul speak to us as brothers and sisters in Christ.
Paul urges us to respond to God's mercy.
We must offer our bodies to God as our bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit.
We must offer our bodies as living sacrifices.
At the time of Moses, animals were killed for sacrifice, so those were not living sacrifices.
Whereas we offer our bodies alive to God as living sacrifices.
We offer our bodies as a sacrifice to God because we are priests to our God and priests offer sacrifices.
If we offer our bodies to God, our sacrifice is holy.
God is pleased if we offer our bodies to God.
Just as the priests of Levi performed their spiritual service of worship in the temple of God, so offering our bodies to God is our spiritual service of worship.

passages.scripture: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.

lines.text: God is holy and merciful.
God calls us to live differently from the world.
Do not conform to the ways of this world.
Let God change you inside.
Let your mind be renewed.
Test to see what the will of God.
When your mind is renewed and then you test God’s will, then you will be able to approve God’s will.
God’s will is good.
God’s will pleases Him.
God’s will is perfect.

passages.scripture: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.

lines.text: God gave Paul grace.
Paul speaks to each of us because of the grace God gave Paul.
We must not think of ourselves more highly than we should.
We must think about ourselves with sober judgment.
God has given each of us a measure of faith.
We must judge ourselves according to the faith God has given us.

passages.scripture: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function, so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.

lines.text: Each person has a body.
Our bodies have many parts.
For example, we all have heads, necks and chests.
And not all parts of our bodies do the same thing.
In the same way, we are many people in Christ.
And, together, all Christians are one body in Christ.
Each of us is a part of this body.
Each of us belongs to each other.

passages.scripture: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith; if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach; if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

lines.text: God gives each of us grace.
God gives us different gifts.
Each person receives gifting from God.
Some people receive the gift of prophecy.
If you have the gift of prophecy, use it according to your faith.
Some people receive the gift of serving.
If you have the gift of serving, then serve.
Some people receive the gift of teaching.
If you have the gift of teaching, then teach.
Some people receive the gift of encouragement.
If you have the gift of encouragement, then encourage others.
Some people receive the gift of giving.
If you have the gift of giving, then give generously.
Some people receive the gift of leadership.
If you have the gift of leadership, then lead with diligence.
Some people receive the gift of showing mercy.
If you have the gift of showing mercy, the show mercy cheerfully.

passages.scripture: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.

lines.text: Love must be sincere.
Do not pretend to love.
Do not wear the clothing of love while inwardly you are full of hatred.
Hate what is evil.
Hold tightly to what is good.

passages.scripture: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.

lines.text: Us Christians must have deep love for each other as brothers and sisters.
We must honor each other more than you honor yourselves.
We must give more respect to others than we receive.

passages.scripture: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

lines.text: We must not become lazy in our zeal.
We must keep our spiritual fervor strong.
We must serve the Lord.

passages.scripture: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.

lines.text: While we hope, we must be joyful.
In our affliction, we must be patient for the Lord to save us.
We must pray until God answers.

passages.scripture: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

lines.text: If we are able, we must help other believers who have needs like food and clothes.
We must share what we have with these believers.
We must always look for opportunity to show hospitality.
We must welcome strangers into our homes.

passages.scripture: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

lines.text: Some people will persecute us.
We bless those who persecute us.
We do not curse those who persecute us.
Instead of cursing, we bless.
Regarding blessing and not cursing, in 1 Corinthians Paul says if anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse.
Regarding blessing and not cursing, in 2 Timothy Paul says Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to Paul and the Lord will repay Alexander according to his deeds.

passages.scripture: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

lines.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice.
Weep with those who weep.
We must be sympathetic and empathetic toward others, sharing in their joys and sorrows.

passages.scripture: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

lines.text: We must live in harmony with each other.
We must not be proud.
We must spend time with humble people.
We must not be wise in our own eyes.

passages.scripture: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

lines.text: If someone does evil to us, we must not do evil back to them.
We must not repay evil to people who have done evil to us.
Do not return harm when someone harms you.
Think carefully about what is good.
And do what is right in the eyes of all people.
We use our freedom in Christ to not only do right in the eyes of God, but, if possible, also do right in the eyes of people.

passages.scripture: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

lines.text: If it is possible, then live at peace with all people.
However, someone else may refuse to live in peace with us, so then peace may not be possible.
If there must be a lack of peace, then it should be the fault of others, and not our fault for the lack of peace.
We should not be responsible for lack of peace.

passages.scripture: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

lines.text: We are beloved.
We must not take revenge on anyone who has wronged us.
We must trust God and allow Him to be angry and to judge.
We do not repay evil; God repays as He wills.
We trust God to repay any evil and do not repay evil ourselves.
God says that vengeance belongs to Him, not to us.
God says that He is the One who repays vengeance, not us.
Instead of repaying evil ourselves, we should leave an empty space for God to repay wrath, if that is His will.

passages.scripture: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

lines.text: If your enemy is hungry, instead of repaying them evil, give them food.
If your enemy is thirsty, instead of repaying them evil, give them something to drink.
In this way we show kindness to our enemies.
By showing kindness, we will heap burning coals on their heads.
Being kind to our enemies may lead our enemies to feel shame and change their ways.

passages.scripture: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

lines.text: Evil exists in the world.
Evil can try to defeat us.
We must not let evil defeat us.
We must not let evil control us.
Goodness is powerful to fight evil.
We use goodness to fight evil.
We defeat evil by doing good, not by repaying evil and not by becoming evil.
